page: The Microsoft Azure D48pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an ARM64-architecture Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. It is configured with 48 dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, paired with 192 GB of RAM, yielding a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Hardware features include AES encryption instructions, a 32 MB L3 cache, and local storage provided by a bundled 1,843 GB SSD.

In synthetic benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-threaded capabilities, registering top-tier performance in multi-core stress testing, Clang software compilation, and high-throughput Redis SET operations reaching 61.96 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core processing metrics, such as single-threaded Geekbench scores and bzip3 decompression rates, fall into lower performance tiers due to the moderate per-core clock rate of the ARM architecture.

From a resource density and architecture standpoint, the D48pds_v5 provides linear core scaling and consistent memory throughput without thread contention. The combination of dedicated ARM cores, system memory, and direct-attached local SSD storage makes this instance cost-effective for multi-threaded microservices, software compilation pipelines, caching layers, and database workloads requiring high multi-core throughput.
